# NEAR Private OTC

> Private OTC deal board on NEAR testnet. The board is open to everyone and shows pair, side, expiry, status, request and counter-offer counts only. To see terms a taker requests access: they must hold at least $200 (CoinGecko) of the token the maker wants, wallet + verifier; a fixed spam filter independent of deal size, not a fill guarantee, then the maker approves (or auto-approves anyone with funds). Sign in with email/Google (Privy) or a NEAR wallet (Meteor, HOT, Intear, HERE, MyNearWallet; Ledger without message signing). Deals can be public (listed on the board) or private (link only, never listed; maker can switch private to public, not back). Expiry options: 2 min (demo), 1h, 24h, 7d, enforced by the verifier via the signed intent deadline. Exact terms and counter-offers are sealed to an OutLayer TEE enclave and revealed only to approved requesters. Matching NEP-413 signed token_diff intents settle atomically via execute_intents on a NEAR Intents verifier (otcdesk-intents.testnet).

## Key facts
- Verifier: otcdesk-intents.testnet (near/intents defuse v0.4.2 release wasm)
- Relayer: otcdesk.testnet
- Tokens: otcdesk-usdc.testnet (tUSDC), otcdesk-eth.testnet (tETH), wrap.testnet (wNEAR)
- Enclave: OutLayer project otcdesk-enclave.testnet/private-otc, pubkey 03312dd677a5864ffc8cff352b7419b90896c9aee20e4f79308c1106517a4947e8
- Sign-in: Privy (Google) → NEAR implicit account, or a NEAR wallet via Wallet Selector; the board needs no sign-in
- Built at NEAR HACKATHON 2026; track: defi (privacy is a supporting feature: terms sealed in OutLayer TDX)

## Pages
- [Board](/app): open deals (coarse info)
- [New deal](/app/new)
- [My deals](/app/mine)
- [Wallet](/app/wallet): verifier balances, faucet (tUSDC, tETH, wNEAR), deposit from your wallet (NEAR-wallet sign-ins), withdraw to your own NEAR account (everyone, signed ft_withdraw intent), activity
- Balances are held in the NEAR Intents verifier. Deposits and withdrawals are public on chain, and settled trades are visible on chain; open deal terms stay sealed.
- Testnet trust note: the verifier otcdesk-intents.testnet is our own unmodified copy of NEAR Intents defuse v0.4.2, and its super-admin is otcdesk.testnet (the operator). So on testnet the operator could in theory upgrade the contract or move balances held in it. On mainnet, settlement would use the official intents.near.
- [How it works](/app/how): flow, privacy, every NEAR feature used

## API
- GET /api/health
- GET /api/prices — reference USD prices (CoinGecko, cached 30 s)
- GET /api/deals — public board
- GET /api/deals/{id}

Faucet: 1000 tUSDC, 50 wNEAR, 0.5 tETH per claim, 3 claims per token per day, credited straight into your verifier balance. One claim of any token clears the $200 request threshold at current prices.

## Try it as an agent
Everything below is plain HTTP against the site serving this file (`U=` its origin; paths below are relative to it) plus the helpers in `shared/otc.mjs` (`signIntent`, `intentPayload`, `tokenDiff`, `seal`, `tokenById`, `toUnits`, `b64`, `ENCLAVE_PUBKEY`).

1. **Make a testnet key.** Generate an ed25519 keypair. Your account is the NEAR implicit account = the 32-byte public key as hex. See: an account id like `3f9a…` (64 hex chars).
2. **Sign in.** Sign a NEP-413 message with `signIntent({ message: JSON.stringify({ otc_login: <account>, ts: Date.now() }), nonce: <32 random bytes>, recipient: "near-private-otc" }, <pubkey base58>, sign)`, then
   `POST /api/auth/wallet` with body `{ "signed": <that signed object> }`. See: `{ "token": "…" }`. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every call below (session lasts 24 h).
3. **Get test funds.** `POST /api/faucet` with body `{ "account": <account>, "token": "tUSDC" }` (also `"tETH"`, `"wNEAR"`). See: the claim result; 1000 tUSDC, 0.5 tETH or 50 wNEAR land straight in your verifier balance. Limit 3 claims per token per day (429 after that).
4. **Build the intent.** For selling e.g. 150 tUSDC for 60 wNEAR: `terms = { sell_token, sell_amount: toUnits("150", dec), buy_token, buy_amount: toUnits("60", dec) }` (ids and decimals from `tokenById`), then
   `intent = await signIntent(intentPayload({ signer: <account>, intents: [tokenDiff(sell_token, sell_amount, buy_token, buy_amount)], deadlineMs: Date.now() + 3600e3, nonce }), <pubkey base58>, sign)`. The deadline is your expiry; the verifier enforces it.
5. **Seal and post.** `offer = { v: 1, deal: <16 chars from 23456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz>, from: <account>, to: "*", terms, note: "", intent }`, then
   `POST /api/deals` with body `{ "offer_ct": seal(ENCLAVE_PUBKEY, offer), "nonce": b64(nonce), "account": <account>, "visibility": "public" }` (or `"private"`). The keeper asks the OutLayer enclave to check it on chain, which can take a while. See: `{ id, pair, side, deadline, status: "Open", check_tx, … }` with no size or price.
6. **Check the board.** `GET /api/deals` (no sign-in). See: your deal listed by `id` with pair, side and expiry only; `GET /api/deals/<id>` for one deal, or open `/d/<id>` in a browser.

Errors come back as JSON with an HTTP status, e.g. 400 if the expiry is already past or the offer isn't signed by you and open to `*`.

### Take a deal as an agent (do X - see Y)
Continue from steps 1-3 with a second key (the taker). It needs at least $200 of the token the maker wants; one faucet claim is enough.

7. **Find a deal.** `GET /api/deals` - see open deals with `id`, `pair`, `side`, `deadline`, `auto_approve`. No size or price.
8. **Request the terms.** `request_ct = seal(ENCLAVE_PUBKEY, { wallet: <your signed login from step 2>, account, deal: <id> })`, then `POST /api/deals/<id>/request` with `{ request_ct, account }`. See: `{ request: { status: "approved" } }` if the maker turned on auto-approve, else `"pending"` until the maker approves (`403` if you hold less than $200 of the wanted token).
9. **Read the sealed terms.** Make a one-time secp256k1 key (`newKeypair()`), `request_ct = seal(ENCLAVE_PUBKEY, { wallet, eph_pub: <its pub>, account, deal })`, `POST /api/deals/<id>/reveal` with `{ request_ct, account }`. See: `offers_ct`; `unseal(<its sk>, offers_ct)` gives the offers you may see, the opening one has `to: "*"` and exact `terms`.
10. **Accept.** Sign the mirror intent (sell what the maker buys, buy what the maker sells, same amounts, deadline = the opening offer's `deadline`), seal `{ v: 1, deal, from: you, to: <maker>, terms, note: "", intent }`, and `POST /api/deals/<id>/offer` with `{ offer_ct, nonce, account, kind: "accept", reply_to: "o1" }`. See: `{ settled: true, tx }`; the enclave checked the exact match and the relayer ran `execute_intents`. A second accept gets `409 Too late`.
11. **Post with auto-approve (maker side).** Add `"auto_approval": <NEP-413 signed {"otc_approve": <deal id>, "requester": "*"}, recipient "near-private-otc">` to the `POST /api/deals` body in step 5. See: `auto_approve: true` on the board.
12. **Cancel (maker side).** For each live offer nonce sign `intentPayload({ signer, intents: [], deadlineMs: now + 10 min, nonce })` and `POST /api/deals/<id>/cancel` with `{ account, signed: [...] }`. See: `{ tx }`; the nonces are burned on the verifier.

### Run the ready-made agents
- **Two agents, one trade:** `U=<APP_URL> node scripts/agents/run.mjs` - see a maker and a taker agent with fresh implicit accounts sign in, use the faucet, post, discover, request, read the terms and settle; every step prints a NearBlocks link. About 70 s.
- **N agents racing:** `TAKERS=3 U=<APP_URL> node scripts/agents/run.mjs` - see several takers read the same deal; the first accept settles, the rest get a 409 ("settling right now" or "Too late"). Each extra taker costs 3 more OutLayer enclave calls.
- **Sub-account agents:** `PARENT_ID=<your>.testnet PARENT_KEY=ed25519:<key> U=<APP_URL> node scripts/agents/run.mjs --subaccounts` - see each agent get its own sub-account `maker-xxxx.<your>.testnet` (0.05 NEAR from the parent), register its key on the verifier with `add_public_key`, then trade. It also adds a function-call key limited to the verifier and shows that this key is refused at sign-in.
- Code: `scripts/agents/lib.mjs` (an `Agent` class: `signIn`, `faucet`, `postDeal`, `requestTerms`, `readTerms`, `accept`, `cancel`) and `scripts/agents/run.mjs`.

### Sub-accounts and limited keys: what works
- **Works:** an agent on a named sub-account with its own full-access key. The parent creates it with a small balance; the agent registers its key on the verifier once (`add_public_key`, 1 yoctoNEAR) because the verifier only knows implicit-account keys by default. The parent can delete the sub-account later.
- **Doesn't work:** function-call (limited) access keys. The app's sign-in and the enclave's own check (`key_belongs` in `enclave/src/nearauth.rs`) accept only full-access keys of named accounts, and the deployed enclave can't change right now. A function-call key also can't attach the 1 yoctoNEAR that `add_public_key` needs.
- So the limit is the sub-account's balance, not the key type: keep only what the agent may lose in its verifier balance.

### Agent safety
- Use a dedicated key, implicit account or sub-account with small funds. Never give an agent your main wallet key.
- The $200 check is a spam filter, not proof that a counterparty can pay.
- Auto-approve reveals your exact terms to anyone who passes that check. Leave it off if you want to choose who sees them.
- Intents settle atomically and only when both sides really hold the funds; otherwise nothing moves. Nothing guarantees a fill or a price.
- A human should set the agent's limits (pairs, max size, price bounds) and review its trades. Testnet only.
